column4: flat 7+1 spacetime, the example of the author's document (m = 1, G_S = -1e5, G_V = +1e4, k_F = 0.756636150701493 in seven space dimensions): this program gives M = 0.348097340146, rho = 1.388100213e-5, eps = 1.348787233e-5, E/A - m = -0.02832142796, and finds the saturation point (the minimum of the energy per particle, where the pressure vanishes: p = -4.2e-22) at k_F = 0.756636150701; the document prints 0.348097340146, 1.388100213e-5, 1.348787233e-5, -0.02832142796 and 0.756636150701493. Largest relative difference 1.7e-10

thermodynamic consistency of the Kohn-Sham state (flat, seven space dimensions): the pressure computed from the momentum integral, <k^2/(7 w)> + Pi, equals mu rho - eps with mu = sqrt(k_F^2 + M^2) + G_V rho along the whole equation of state (141 Fermi momenta for each of the two sets; largest deviation 7.7e-16 of eps); at saturation the chemical potential equals the energy per particle (theorem of Hugenholtz and Van Hove): mu - E/A = 3.3e-16. With the exchange terms (G_0 = -98750, G_1 = 20000) the lowest energy per particle is E/A - m = 0.000156 at k_F = 0.0200: in Hartree-Fock the doubled vector repulsion removes the binding: matter is not self-bound for these couplings

the momentum integral over the ellipsoid of occupied states (four flat and three deflating directions; 115200 nodes): at the reference time (all stretch factors 1) it reproduces the integral over the ball in seven dimensions, M, rho and eps to 2.2e-14 and the pressures along flat and deflating directions to 3.3e-15 of the kinetic energy density; with 401408 nodes instead, M, eps and the pressures change by at most 9.2e-10 (relative) at the clock readings 1.5, 3 and 4 for both sets of rates

conservation of energy on the deflating 7+1 spacetime: the Kohn-Sham energy density obeys d eps/dx4 = sum_t rate_t (eps + p_t) with the pressures p_t = <s_t^2 u_t^2/w> + Pi along the deflating coordinates (the covariant divergence of the energy-momentum tensor vanishes); numerical derivative against the right-hand side at the clock readings -1, 0, 0.7, 2 and 3.5, for equal rates and for rates in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3: largest relative deviation 5.6e-9

history of saturated matter while x5, x6, x7 deflate (7+1, all momenta, collisionless; equal rates / rates 1 : 2 : 3): the density grows as exp(tau_d); the mass of the particles falls to half its value at the reference time at tau_d = 0.983 / 0.990; the matter is self-bound (energy per particle below m) only for -0.675 < tau_d < 0.537 / -0.658 < tau_d < 0.523; at tau_d = 4 the vector repulsion (1/2) G_V rho^2 is 69.4 / 65.0 per cent of the energy density, which then grows as exp(2 tau_d); the collisionless state lies above the state of lowest energy of the same density by at most 8.652e-1 m per particle on -2 <= tau_d <= 4 (energy that collisions would turn into heat)

fields that do not depend on x5, x6, x7: the reduced couplings grow as exp(tau_d), and uniform matter becomes self-bound when the scalar attraction reaches a threshold (verified: bound 0.1 per cent above it, not bound 0.1 per cent below it). Thresholds in units m = 1: D = 4, scalar attraction alone (G_V = 0): |G_S| m^3 = 62.0767; D = 4, G_V = 0.1 |G_S| (the author's example, Hartree): |G_S| m^3 = 85.6504; D = 4, the author's example with exchange terms (Hartree-Fock): |G_S| m^3 = 119.5723; D = 3, scalar attraction alone (G_V = 0): |G_S| m^2 = 8.0671; D = 3, G_V = 0.1 |G_S| (the author's example, Hartree): |G_S| m^2 = 9.8364; D = 3, the author's example with exchange terms (Hartree-Fock): |G_S| m^2 = 12.2272. The deflation therefore turns a gas into self-bound matter at the clock reading tau_bind = ln(|G_S|(threshold)/|G_S|(reference))

covariant form of the interaction on 4+4 (the two halves W = +1 and W = -1 carry opposite scalar and vector charge): for the attractive scalar coupling of the author's example (g_1 = -0.1 g_0) the state with equal halves is never the state of lowest energy; matter polarizes spontaneously. Polarization P = (rho_+ - rho_-)/rho of the state of lowest energy, for couplings 1.5, 3 and 6 times the binding threshold of the quantized-sector form and total densities of Fermi momentum 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0 (in this order): 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 0.35, 1.00, 1.00, 0.65, 0.20, 1.00, 1.00, 0.40, 0.20 (grid of 0.05). The fully polarized state is the Kohn-Sham state of one kind of particle with four states and the couplings G_S0 + G_0, G_V0 + G_1 (verified to 1e-9). Example: for couplings three times the binding threshold of the quantized-sector form and total density of Fermi momentum 0.8: E/A - m = +0.3799 for equal halves, +0.3731 for all particles in one half, and +0.1323 in the quantized-sector form

the Kohn-Sham method and the CJT effective potential agree (no-sea approximation): for 30 states (five sets of parameters in D = 7, 4, 3; Fermi momenta 0.3 to 1.4) the stationary point of Omega(M, V_0; mu) at the chemical potential of the Kohn-Sham state has the same mass, density and energy density, and -Omega equals the Kohn-Sham pressure (sum of the four relative deviations at most 1.6e-12; residuals of the two stationarity conditions at most 8.2e-15). Of the 23 states with positive pressure, 20 are the global minimum of Omega; in the other 3 a denser phase has the higher pressure at the same chemical potential (the Kohn-Sham state of that density is then metastable: a dilute gas above saturated matter)

with the filled states of negative energy (cutoff Lambda) a massless field acquires a mass in vacuum when the scalar attraction exceeds the critical coupling G_c = -(2 pi)^D (D - 1)/(NU A_D Lambda^(D-1)) (A_D: area of the unit sphere): G_c Lambda^6 = -90 pi^4 for D = 7 (the value of the author's document DIRAC16COMPLEX), G_c Lambda^3 = -3 pi^2 for D = 4, G_c Lambda^2 = -pi^2/2 for D = 3; the minimization of the effective potential gives no mass 2 per cent below G_c and a mass 2 per cent above it, for all three D. On the deflating spacetime the reduced coupling crosses G_c at the clock reading tau_c = ln(G_c/G_S(reference))

the Dirac sea and the author's example. The coupling G_S = -1e5 m^-6 of the example exceeds the critical coupling 90 pi^4/Lambda^6 of the vacuum as soon as the cutoff is larger than Lambda = (90 pi^4/1e5)^(1/6) m = 0.6665 m: the no-sea approximation presupposes a cutoff below this value. With the sea included (bare mass adjusted so that the vacuum mass stays 1): without sea: saturation at k_F = 0.7566, M = 0.3481, E/A - M_vac = -0.02832; Lambda = 0.3: bare mass 0.9979, saturation at k_F = 0.7566, M = 0.3479, E/A - M_vac = -0.02837; Lambda = 0.45: bare mass 0.9660, saturation at k_F = 0.7568, M = 0.3438, E/A - M_vac = -0.02984; Lambda = 0.6: bare mass 0.7578, saturation at k_F = 0.7565, M = 0.3072, E/A - M_vac = -0.04483

contact interaction, bare mass and Vorton-Scalar together: for f_D = 0 and G_S = G_V = 0 the functional is the one of the main project (masses and energy densities for C = 4, 6, 10 and k_F = 0.3, 0.6, 1.0 agree to 2.1e-8), and the smallest C at which matter is self-bound is 3.701101 here against 3.701102 there

at low density the Vorton-Scalar acts on the mass of the fermions exactly as a scalar contact coupling of strength -C = -g_VS^2/m_s^2 (units m = 1), whatever fraction of the mass is a bare mass: (M - 1)/rho_S tends to G_S - C (five sets of parameters; at k_F <= 0.05 the deviation is at most 1.8e-4). The exchange of the radial mode of the scalar and the scalar channel g_0 of the self-interaction are the same interaction at momenta far below m_s

a bare Dirac mass gives the phase mode of the Vorton-Scalar a mass. The chiral symmetry U(1)_VS is then broken explicitly; for the phase theta of the scalar the fermions have the mass m(theta) = sqrt(m_D^2 + m_Y^2 + 2 m_D m_Y cos(theta)) (m_Y = g_VS v_VS), and the energy of the filled states gives m_ph^2 v_VS^2 = (|<psibar psi>| - rho_S) m_D m_Y/m, the relation of Gell-Mann, Oakes and Renner with the scalar density rho_S of the matter subtracted (numerical second derivative against this formula, 24 cases, and the closed form of the condensate for D = 3, (nu/(2 pi^2)) [Lambda sqrt(Lambda^2 + m^2) - m^2 asinh(Lambda/m)] m/2: largest deviation 3.2e-7 of the vacuum value). In units of the couplings of the model, m_ph^2 = C m_s^2 f_D (|<psibar psi>| - rho_S)/((1 - f_D) m^3): on the deflating spacetime m_ph grows as exp(tau_d/2), and its value depends on the cutoff Lambda through the condensate. In matter the mass falls, m_ph^2(k_F)/m_ph^2(0) = 1 - rho_S(k_F)/|<psibar psi>|: Lambda = 1 m: |<psibar psi>| = 0.10798 m^3, ratio 0.8540 at k_F = Lambda/2; Lambda = 2 m: |<psibar psi>| = 0.61370 m^3, ratio 0.8241 at k_F = Lambda/2; Lambda = 4 m: |<psibar psi>| = 2.91759 m^3, ratio 0.7897 at k_F = Lambda/2. The ratio vanishes only at k_F = Lambda (6.7e-16), where the filled states of positive energy cancel those of negative energy below the cutoff: that is the limit of the effective theory and not a prediction
